title: Component dimensions of an integral locally finite type scheme over a valuation domain
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation domain, meaning an integral domain such that every nonzero element of $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ or its inverse belongs to $A$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$ and residue field $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$. Let $h:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a morphism locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism; def-weil-affine-spectrum], where $Z$ is an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and suppose $h(\eta)$ is the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $Z_K=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $Z_k=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k$ be its generic and closed fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Both fibres are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Then $Z_K$ is integral and its generic point maps to $\eta$. For every irreducible component $E$ of $Z_k$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $z$, one has $\dim_z(Z_k)=\dim E=\dim Z_K$, where $\dim$ is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and $\dim_z$ is local topological dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Empty $Z_k$ is allowed, in which case the component assertion is vacuous. No Noetherianity or rank condition on $A$, quasi-compactness of $Z$, or flatness hypothesis on $h$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose an affine open cover of $Z$ by nonempty $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ for which $B$ is finite type over $A$, as permitted by local finite type. Integrality makes every such $B$ a domain. The generic point $\eta$ belongs to every nonempty open: otherwise its closed complement would contain $\overline{\{\eta\}}=Z$. Its prime in $B$ is $(0)$, since $V((0))=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The image of this prime in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $(0)$ by hypothesis, so the inverse image of $(0)\subset B$ is zero. Thus $A\to B$ is injective, and $B$ contains $A$ as a subring.

source.place: Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible), applied to the affine neighbourhoods in Tag 00QK; generic-point and injectivity reduction

proof.text: For $L=K$ and $L=k$, restriction of the fibre to $U$ is the open subscheme $U_L=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A L)$, by open fibre products and the affine tensor-product formula. These opens cover $Z_L$. If $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ generate $B$ over $A$, the elements $b_i\otimes1$ generate $B\otimes_A L$ over $L$: expand a pure tensor $P(b_1,\ldots,b_r)\otimes\lambda$ as the same polynomial in $b_i\otimes1$ with coefficients in $L$, and then add pure tensors. Thus both fibre morphisms are locally of finite type. Every field is Noetherian, since its ideals are only zero and the unit ideal. The finite-type-algebra Noetherian theorem therefore makes every $B\otimes_A L$ Noetherian, and the affine covers show that both fibres are locally Noetherian. Zero chart rings cause no problem.

Set $S=A\setminus\{0\}$. The localization base-change theorem gives $B\otimes_A K\cong S^{-1}B$. No element of $S$ vanishes in $B$, by step 1. In this localization $b/s=0$ forces $tb=0$ for some $t\in S$, hence $b=0$; and a product of two nonzero fractions cannot vanish because $B$ is a domain. Thus $S^{-1}B$ is a nonzero domain, and its zero prime contracts to the zero prime of $B$. Its generic point consequently maps to $\eta$.

source.place: Tags 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), 00ES (lemma-irreducible); the fraction calculation for the generic fibre

proof.text: Each $U_K$ is reduced by the affine reducedness criterion. Reducedness of $Z_K$ follows directly from the stalk definition: any point lies in such an open, where its local ring is reduced, and restriction to an open leaves that stalk unchanged. The fibre projection is a homeomorphism onto $h^{-1}((0))$, so the points above $\eta$ in all these charts are one point $\eta_K$. In each chart its closure is the whole chart, by step 3 and the formula $\overline{\{(0)\}}=V((0))$. Hence its closure in $Z_K$ contains the covering charts and equals $Z_K$. A space with a dense point is irreducible: any closed covering has one member containing that point and hence its whole closure. Therefore $Z_K$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, and is integral. Its generic point $\eta_K$ maps to $\eta$.

Write $d=\dim Z_K$. This is the dimension of an integral scheme locally of finite type over the field $K$, by steps 2 and 4. Every chart $U_K$ is nonempty by step 3. The nonempty-open dimension theorem therefore gives $\dim U_K=d$ for every chosen $U$. Via the affine isomorphism of step 2, homeomorphism invariance and the spectrum/ring dimension equality give $\dim(B\otimes_A K)=d$.

source.place: Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), part (3), for the generic fibre

proof.text: Whenever $U_k\ne\varnothing$, its ring $B\otimes_A k$ is nonzero. Apply the valuation-domain fibre-dimension theorem to the domain inclusion $A\subset B$ from step 1. All its hypotheses hold: $A$ is a valuation domain, $B$ is a finite type $A$-algebra and a domain, and the closed tensor fibre is nonzero. Its equidimensionality conclusion says that every irreducible component of $U_k$ has dimension $\dim(B\otimes_A K)=d$, using step 5 and the homeomorphism of step 2.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), including equidimensionality; More on Morphisms Tag 0GSI, first proof paragraph

proof.text: Let $E$ be an irreducible component of $Z_k$ with generic point $z$, and choose a chart $U$ containing its image in $Z$. Then $z\in U_k$, and the open-component intersection theorem makes $E\cap U_k$ an irreducible component of $U_k$, so step 6 gives $\dim(E\cap U_k)=d$. Give the closed subset $E$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure $E_{\mathrm{red}}$. The closed immersion identifies its topological space with $E$; it is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral. That immersion is locally of finite type, and composition with $Z_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. Apply the nonempty-open dimension theorem to the inverse image of $U_k$ in $E_{\mathrm{red}}$. Homeomorphism invariance identifies the resulting equality with $\dim E=\dim(E\cap U_k)=d$. This use of the field theorem does not require $E$ or $Z$ to be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), part (3), on the component; Schemes Tag 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme); Morphisms Tags 01T5 and 01T3

proof.text: For this $z\in U_k=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A k)$, the affine dimension-at-a-point formula identifies $\dim_z U_k$ with the maximum of the dimensions of its irreducible components through $z$. This formula applies because the chart ring is finite type over the field $k$ by step 2; its statement guarantees that the maximum is over a nonempty family. Every one of these component dimensions is $d$ by step 6, so $\dim_z U_k=d$. Local topological dimension is unchanged on restricting to the open neighbourhood $U_k\subset Z_k$, giving $\dim_z Z_k=d=\dim E=\dim Z_K$. When $Z_k$ is empty there is no $E$ or $z$ to consider; the generic-fibre and local-Noetherian assertions already hold by steps 2--4.

It splits the item into 8 steps, keeps the statement unchanged and adds no new nodes. Sources: Stacks 00QK (algebra.tex:31380) states that Spec(S⊗k) is equidimensional of dimension dim(S⊗K) for a finite-type domain S containing a valuation ring R. Stacks 0GSI (more-morphisms.tex:5188) applies 00QK to the integral Y'. The item is the scheme-level form of that application and is true. Small cases checked: A a field (trivial), Z=Spec A[1/π] (empty closed fibre, clause vacuous), A[x,y]/(xy−π) (two lines of dimension 1). Step by step: (1) the cover of lft/integral charts and the zero prime via spec-irreducible-closed (2) give A⊂B. (2) Open fibre product and the affine tensor formula give the fibre charts; Hilbert basis and the cover definition give locally Noetherian fibres. (3) Localization base change with R=A, M=A∖0 gives S⁻¹B, a nonzero domain. (4) The stalk definition of reduced and the fibre homeomorphism give one dense point η_K, so Z_K is integral. (5) The 0A21(3) node gives dim(B⊗K)=d. (6) All hypotheses of lem-trf-valuation-domain-fibre-dimensions are checked, and its equidimensionality clause is used. (7) The component E: E∩U_k is a component of U_k by open-injection, E_red is integral via the reduced induced subscheme and the closed-immersion homeomorphism, it is lft via 01T5 and clause (e) of the permanence node, and the open-dimension theorem gives dim E=d without quasi-compactness. (8) The 00OT node gives the local dimension as a maximum over a nonempty family; the open-subspace node passes to Z_k. proof_deps equals the union of uses, and every cited statement says what the step takes from it. The DAG search for 00QK finds no duplicate: the affine node is cited, and the other hits are proof pieces or flat/finitely presented variants. I accept the 4 declared tool_uses (integral lft open dimension, reduced induced subscheme, dimension at a point by components, dimension at a point on an open subspace) as generic black boxes.
